fields.label: Rate limits (calls)
fields.description: Every limit on this page is a TOKEN BUCKET, not a quota that resets. A budget is a bucket that refills continuously — its rate spread evenly across its window, every second — up to a maximum it can hold. A caller may spend a full bucket at once, and is then paced at the refill rate rather than blocked until a period rolls over. A refusal carries Retry-After, calculated from exactly how long the bucket needs to afford the request. Reading a rate as "N per day, then blocked" is the one common misreading: it is N per day sustained, arriving continuously.

fields.label: Window (seconds)
fields.description: The period the call rate is expressed over. The bucket refills continuously across it — rate divided by window, every second — never in one step at the end.

fields.label: Per-token Rate (calls/window)
fields.description: The sustained number of calls one partner may keep making, expressed per window. At 120 per 60 seconds the bucket refills 2 calls a second. 0 removes the limit.

fields.label: Per-token Burst (calls)
fields.description: How much this bucket can hold — what one partner may fire at once after a quiet spell, before the sustained rate takes over. Blank allows 240, and it is never less than the rate.

fields.label: Global Rate (calls/window)
fields.description: The sustained number of calls all partners together may keep making, expressed per window. Refusal by this bucket is a 503, not a 429: the caller is not at fault. 0 removes the limit.

fields.label: Global Burst (calls)
fields.description: How much the shared bucket can hold — what all partners together may fire at once after a quiet spell. Blank allows 600, and it is never less than the global rate.

fields.label: Rate limits (bulk calls)
fields.description: Bulk calls have their own bucket, because a bulk write holds its records until it finishes and two running at once contend. Every *_list endpoint draws on this bucket too — lead_list, activity_list, file_list, note_list, call_list — so paging a large result set is paced by these numbers and NOT by the row budgets below. A caller reporting repeated 429s while paging is almost always hitting this.

fields.label: Bulk Window (seconds)
fields.description: The period the bulk rate is expressed over. At the shipped 1 per 5 seconds, a second bulk or list call arriving inside 5 seconds of the first is refused.

fields.label: Bulk Rate (calls/window)
fields.description: The number of bulk calls one partner may make per bulk window. 0 removes the limit.

fields.label: Bulk Burst (calls)
fields.description: How much the bulk bucket can hold. Pinned at 1 and refused at any other value: above 1, two concurrent bulk writes deadlock on the lead dedup index and the losing batch is rolled back whole. Raising Bulk Rate is the supported way to buy headroom.

fields.label: Volume limits (rows, sustained rate)
fields.description: How much data may be moved, as opposed to how fast. Reads and writes are counted separately, and a bulk call is charged its true row count exactly as the same rows read one at a time would be. These are SUSTAINED RATES, not daily quotas: a caller may spend the whole budget at once and then continues at the refill rate, so a limit here paces extraction rather than bounding it. Bounding total extraction would need a fixed quota, which this is not.

fields.label: Volume Window (seconds)
fields.description: The period the row rates are expressed over. Blank uses one day. The bucket refills continuously across it, so an emptied budget returns gradually rather than at a daily reset.

fields.label: Per-token Read Rows/window
fields.description: The sustained number of rows one partner may read, expressed per window. At 10000 per day that is about 7 rows a minute returning to an emptied bucket, so a caller who drains it is paced, never blocked until tomorrow. 0 removes the limit.

fields.label: Global Read Rows/window
fields.description: The sustained number of rows all partners together may read, expressed per window. 0 removes the limit.

fields.label: Per-token Write Rows/window
fields.description: The sustained number of rows one partner may create or update, expressed per window. 0 removes the limit.

fields.label: Global Write Rows/window
fields.description: The sustained number of rows all partners together may create or update, expressed per window. 0 removes the limit.

fields.label: Bulk Max Records
fields.description: The largest number of records one bulk upload may carry. An upload above this is refused.

fields.label: Bulk Max Files
fields.description: The largest number of files one bulk upload may carry. Files are limited more tightly than rows, because each one is scanned and saved.

fields.label: List Max Page
fields.description: The largest number of records returned by a single read.

fields.label: List Default Page
fields.description: The number of records returned when the caller does not ask for an amount.

fields.label: File Download Timeout (seconds)
fields.description: The time spent fetching a file from a partner's link before giving up.

fields.label: File Download Max Size (MB)
fields.description: The largest file accepted from a partner's link, in megabytes. A larger one is refused.

fields.label: Idempotency Window (hours)
fields.description: The time a request's saved answer is kept. A repeat of the same request within it is answered from the saved copy instead of being written again.

fields.label: Async bulk jobs
fields.description: A second, background tier for high-volume creates. A partner submits a job and is told when it finishes. It stays off until it is switched on.

fields.label: Inline Job Max Records
fields.description: The largest number of records accepted in one job sent as text.

fields.label: File Job Max Records
fields.description: The largest number of records accepted in one uploaded file job.

fields.label: File Job Max Size (MB)
fields.description: The largest uploaded job file accepted, in megabytes. A larger one is refused before it is stored.

fields.label: Jobs Processed At Once
fields.description: The number of jobs processed at the same time in the background. Held at one, so bulk creates run in turn.

fields.label: Concurrent Jobs Per Partner
fields.description: The number of jobs one partner may have waiting or running. A further submission is refused until one finishes.

fields.label: Max Queued Jobs
fields.description: The largest number of jobs that may be waiting or running across all partners. A submission beyond it is asked to retry later.

fields.label: Chunk Size
fields.description: Records are saved in batches of this size while a job runs. A bigger batch finishes the job sooner; a smaller one loses less work if the job stops halfway.

fields.label: Job Timeout (seconds)
fields.description: The time a single job is allowed to run. A job still going past this is stopped and marked failed.

fields.label: Results Retention (days)
fields.description: The age at which a finished job and its per-record results are deleted.

fields.label: Silence alert
fields.description: An email when a watched partner stops sending leads. Dormant until the automation `Notify::Partner::silence` is armed, and it in turn needs request logging on — silence and not-logging are indistinguishable, so it stays quiet rather than guess. Which partners are watched is a tick on each CRM Lead API Mapping.

fields.label: Silence Hours
fields.description: How long a watched partner may send nothing before one email is sent. Minimum 1. Blank uses 8. One email per quiet spell, and it re-arms by itself when the partner sends again.

fields.label: Silence Alert Recipients
fields.description: Who is told, comma separated. Blank sends nothing, which is how the alert ships. The message goes out through the site's default outgoing email account, like every other mail this app sends.

fields.label: Async bulk volume
fields.description: The row budget for the background tier, kept separate so a large load cannot spend the live one. A sustained rate like the others, not a daily allowance.

fields.label: Per-token Async Rows/day
fields.description: The number of rows one partner may write per day through the background tier.

fields.label: Global Async Rows/day
fields.description: The number of rows all partners together may write per day through the background tier.
